results.hypothesis: The feature activates on the second token of split compounds or phrasal forms where a short preposition/adverb is attached to the previous word by punctuation, such as "onto the" or "city-wide".
positive_probes: They launched a city-wide recycling campaign yesterday.
Please move onto the next agenda item.
Our coast-side cottages filled quickly in summer.
She switched over-to manual control after midnight.
The team approved a company-wide hiring freeze.
distractor_probes: They launched a city wide recycling campaign yesterday.
Please move on to the next agenda item.
The team approved a nationwide hiring freeze.

results.hypothesis: The feature detects tokens immediately following a hyphen or after a word ending in a directional particle, especially when the resulting phrase forms a common spatial/layout expression.
positive_probes: Place the icon top-right on the toolbar.
Align the caption left-aligned beneath the photo.
Keep the badge bottom-left near the margin.
Move the legend right-aligned beside the chart.
Set the menu center-left for balance.
distractor_probes: Place the icon in the upper corner.
Align the caption neatly beneath the photo.
Keep the badge near the left margin.

results.hypothesis: The feature responds to line-break or formatting-boundary continuations in prose, where a highly frequent function word or suffix-like continuation token completes the preceding expression across punctuation/newline boundaries.
positive_probes:
She whispered,
and then disappeared into the fog.

The old map ended:
of the valley, nothing remained.

His warning was clear;
to ignore it meant disaster.

I kept the letter—
from my brother—folded away.

Their anthem began,
with a single trembling note.
distractor_probes: She whispered and then disappeared into the fog.
The old map of the valley was badly torn.
Their anthem began with a single trembling note.

results.hypothesis: Token-level feature for the wordpiece/token " the" specifically when it appears as the second part of a merged form like "onto the" (i.e., the model tokenization yields a boundary before "the" inside a larger phrase).
positive_probes: He set the cup onto the shelf.
They walked into the theater quietly.
She looked up to the ceiling fan.
We drove over to the old mill.
The cat ran under the table.
distractor_probes: He set the cup on the shelf.
They walked into theaters quietly.
She looked up toward the ceiling fan.

results.hypothesis: Secondary/polysemantic possibility: activation on the token "wide" when it is the second part of a hyphenated form like "city-wide".
positive_probes: The policy applies company-wide starting next Monday.
They launched a campus-wide recycling initiative this spring.
A city-wide curfew began after the storm.
The update caused system-wide outages for hours.
We conducted a nation-wide survey on healthcare access.
distractor_probes: The road was wide and nearly empty.
They launched a wide-ranging recycling initiative this spring.
A citywide curfew began after the storm.

results.hypothesis: Formatting/newline continuation is not the core feature; if present at all, it is only incidental to specific frequent continuations rather than generic line-break-boundary words.

Continue on the next line if needed.
Boundary words near newlines are not special.
